podcast.body: After a six-year hiatus from making music videos, Pearl Jam eventually returned to the format with the release of the video for "Do the Evolution" in 1998. This marked a shift from their previous stance of refusing to produce clips after their initial singles from the *Ten* album. "Pearl Jam wouldn't do another video until Do the Evolution in 1998."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Future of the Music Video - Part 2

podcast.body: This song and its accompanying music video perfectly embodied the philosophical shift influenced by Rage Against the Machine, representing a transition from introspective feelings to an outward expression against the system. It served as a clear example of Pearl Jam moving beyond conventional Grunge themes. "Tenemos esa canción y sobre todo, ese videoclip de Doodie Evolution que es la filosofía de rechagan semacín por completo, y que tú escuchas el primer álbum de Perlham y escuchas el ten, y ves ahí una evolución más rabiosa hacia el mundo y el sistema."

srcs.episode: Poniendo en su lugar a Rage Against the Machine
